description: Transport layer expansion: transport profiles, adaptive cover traffic, QUIC binding, HTTP/3 and WebTransport, constrained device transport (UDP/DTLS), transport advertisement, and documentation.

gates.name: Transport Profiles and Adaptive Cover Traffic

stories.title: Implement TransportProfile enum and TransportConfig integration
stories.description: Implement the TransportProfile enum with four device-class variants (Server, Desktop, Mobile, Constrained) per §10.13. Each variant bundles default values for min_relays, max_connections, reconnect backoff range, and cover traffic tier. Platform inference via #[cfg(target_os)] selects a default profile at initialization. TransportConfig gains a `profile: TransportProfile` field that drives all profile-aware behavior downstream. This is the foundation story — SCP-251, SCP-252, and SCP-253 all depend on it.
acceptanceCriteria: TransportProfile enum with Server, Desktop, Mobile, Constrained variants in profile.rs
Each variant carries default min_relays (Server=3, Desktop=3, Mobile=2, Constrained=1), max_connections (Server=usize::MAX, Desktop=50, Mobile=10, Constrained=2), reconnect_backoff range

Platform inference via #[cfg(target_os)] with runtime refinement for Linux: headless + >2GB RAM -> Server, <256MB RAM or small arch -> Constrained, fallback -> Desktop. iOS/Android -> Mobile. macOS/Windows -> Desktop
TransportConfig has profile: TransportProfile field with platform-inferred default
profile.rs re-exported from scp-transport/src/lib.rs
Unit test: platform default is Desktop on macOS, profile defaults are correct per variant
actionItems: Create crates/scp-transport/src/profile.rs with TransportProfile enum and default accessors
Add platform inference function using #[cfg(target_os)]

sources.section: ## ADR-036: Transport Profiles and Adaptive Resource Management

stories.title: Implement connection budget enforcement in TransportManager
stories.description: Add connection budget enforcement to TransportManager per §10.13.3. The max_connections value is derived from TransportProfile (Server=unlimited, Desktop=50, Mobile=10, Constrained=2). When the budget is exceeded, the least-recently-used connection is closed. Subscriptions on evicted connections are migrated to surviving connections to the same relay, or trigger relay reassignment if no surviving connection exists. Mobile profile additionally sheds connections for inactive contexts.

sources.section: ## ADR-037: Alternative Transport Bindings (QUIC, WebTransport, UDP/DTLS)

stories.title: Implement QUIC per-operation stream model
stories.description: Implement the per-operation QUIC stream model per §10.14.1. send() opens a bidirectional stream, sends PUBLISH, receives ACK, closes stream. subscribe() opens a long-lived bidirectional stream, sends SUBSCRIBE, receives BLOBs until unsubscribe. query() opens a bidirectional stream, sends QUERY, receives results + query_complete, closes. delete() opens a bidirectional stream, sends DELETE, receives ACK, closes. Same MessagePack wire format as ADR-004.
acceptanceCriteria: send() opens new bidirectional QUIC stream, sends PUBLISH frame, receives ACK/ERR, closes stream
subscribe() opens long-lived bidirectional stream, sends SUBSCRIBE, streams BLOBs until unsubscribe
query() opens bidirectional stream, sends QUERY, receives results + query_complete, closes stream
delete() opens bidirectional stream, sends DELETE, receives ACK/ERR, closes stream
All frames use same MessagePack wire format as ADR-004 (no ref_id needed — response scoped to stream)
Integration tests verify send roundtrip, subscribe+receive, unsubscribe, query, delete, and backfill operations against a real QUIC listener
actionItems: Create streams.rs with stream-per-operation helpers (open, send frame, receive frame, close)

stories.title: Implement QUIC connection lifecycle (0-RTT, migration, reconnect)
stories.description: Implement QUIC connection lifecycle per §10.14.2. 0-RTT connection resumption via session tickets stored across sessions. stories.title: Implement WebTransport WASM client adapter with fallback
stories.description: Implement the browser-side WebTransport adapter per §10.15.3. The WASM binding uses the browser's WebTransport API when available. Fallback chain: attempt WebTransport first, if WebTransport API is unavailable (Safari, older browsers) or connection fails, fall back to WebSocket. Fallback is transparent to TransportAdapter callers — they see a single adapter that handles the negotiation internally.

stories.title: Implement MessagePack-over-DTLS adapter
stories.description: Implement the SCP-native constrained device adapter per §10.16.1. UdpDtlsAdapter implements TransportAdapter using DTLS 1.3 over UDP. Each SCP operation (PUBLISH, QUERY, DELETE) is a DTLS datagram (or datagram sequence for large payloads). subscribe() returns an error — constrained devices use polling via query(). Session resumption via DTLS session tickets avoids full handshake on reconnect. Same MessagePack wire format as ADR-004.

stories.title: Implement CoAP-over-DTLS adapter for IoT interop
stories.description: Implement the CoAP-based constrained device adapter per §10.16.2. CoAP (RFC 7252) provides the framing layer over DTLS. SCP operations map to CoAP methods: POST for PUBLISH, GET for QUERY, DELETE for DELETE. CoAP Observe (RFC 7641) enables lightweight best-effort subscription (server pushes new blobs, but may stop notifying). Interoperable with existing IoT infrastructure (CoAP proxies, LwM2M).
acceptanceCriteria: CoAP framing over DTLS with method mapping: POST -> PUBLISH, GET -> QUERY, DELETE -> DELETE
